description: Agent-DID HTTP verification vectors (RFC-001 §6.5): accepted and rejected requests. Each rejected vector differs from the valid one by a single change and is re-signed when that change touches signed material. Generated by scripts/regenerate-http-verification-vectors.js.
usage: For each vector: build the Signature-Agent DID document from `keys` (every key is a verification method listed under its `relationships`), register it in a resolver, create a client whose clock returns `now` (the vector's own, else `clock`), and verify `request` with `headers` and a fresh nonce store whose own clock returns the same time.`expected` is the verdict and, for a rejection, `reason` is the `HttpSignatureRejection` a detailed verifier reports; `expectedSequence` is the sequence of verdicts (and `expectedReasons` the reasons, null for an accepted one) when the same request is verified repeatedly with ONE nonce store. Unless a vector gives its own, use the default verifier policy (skew 300 s, lifetime 300 s).
keysNote: TEST-ONLY Ed25519 keys. The seeds are public on purpose; they sign nothing real.

vectors.description: The baseline request: every rule holds.
A request without a query signs `@query` as `?`.
An explicit default port (:443) is dropped from `@authority`.
A non-default port stays in `@authority`.
Additional covered components MAY follow the seven required ones.

"@method": POST
"@authority": api.example.com
"@path": /v1/verify
"@query": ?mode=fixture
"content-digest": sha-256=:/7wt/EAngjJdpxEyEA50/1EdFYXdgOTqGW7UvKzj/vI=:
"date": Mon, 01 Jan 2024 00:00:20 GMT
"signature-agent": did:webvh:QmHttpVerifyFixtureScid:verify.example:agents:fixture-bot
"content-type": application/json
"@signature-params": ("@method" "@authority" "@path" "@query" "content-digest" "date" "signature-agent" "content-type");created=1704067220;expires=1704067280;nonce="a36ac89f07c664f989ce3dab9eeecb2b";keyid="did:webvh:QmHttpVerifyFixtureScid:verify.example:agents:fixture-bot#key-1";alg="ed25519";tag="agent-did"

vectors.description: The `@signature-params` line is re-serialized from the parsed `Signature-Input`: extra spaces between the covered components do not change the signature base.
Header field names are matched case-insensitively.
No `Signature` header.
No `Signature-Input` header.
No `Signature-Agent` header.
No `Date` header (the signature covers it).
No `Content-Digest` header.
The body differs from the one `Content-Digest` was computed over.
`Content-Digest` uses `sha-512` instead of `sha-256`.
`Content-Digest` is a dictionary with `sha-256` and `sha-512`; the profile allows exactly one member, `sha-256`.
`tag="web-bot-auth"`: another profile must not be accepted as an Agent-DID signature.
No `tag` parameter.
`alg="ecdsa-p256-sha256"` on an Ed25519 signature.
No `alg` parameter.
No `nonce` parameter.
An empty `nonce`.
No `created` parameter.
No `expires` parameter.
No `keyid` parameter.
`now` is after `expires`.
`now` equals `expires`.
`created` is later than `now` by more than the allowed skew.
`created` is earlier than `now` by more than the allowed skew.
`created` is earlier than `now` by exactly the allowed skew.
`expires` is earlier than `created` while `now` is still before `expires`.
`expires - created` is 301 seconds with the default lifetime cap.
`expires - created` is exactly 300 seconds.

`keyid` is a key of another DID, not of the `Signature-Agent` DID. The Signature-Agent document even lists that key under assertionMethod and the signature is valid for it, so only the binding rule can reject it.
`keyid` names a fragment the `Signature-Agent` DID document does not have.
`keyid` is a key listed only under `keyAgreement`, and the signature is valid for it.
The signature verifies under key-2, not under the `keyid` key-1.
The last byte of the signature is changed.
`Signature-Input` is not a Structured Field dictionary.
The signature does not cover `@method`.
The signature does not cover `@authority`.
The signature does not cover `@path`.
The signature does not cover `@query`.
The signature does not cover `content-digest`.
The signature does not cover `date`.
The signature does not cover `signature-agent`.
Two required components are swapped (`@path` before `@authority`).
The seven required components in reverse order.
An additional component comes before the required ones; additional components may only follow.

vectors.description: The request method differs from the signed one.
The request host differs from the signed one.
The request path differs from the signed one.
The request query differs from the signed one.
A path and query with percent-encoded octets and every other character the normalized form allows.
A space in the query (it must be sent as %20). The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
A `..` path segment. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
A percent-encoded `..` path segment. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
A non-ASCII character in the path (it must be percent-encoded as UTF-8). The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
An internationalized host name that is not in its ASCII (punycode) form. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
An uppercase host name. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
An uppercase scheme. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
A fragment. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
User information before the host. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
A `?` with an empty query. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
A `'` in the query (it must be sent as %27). The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
A `%` that is not followed by two hex digits. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
Backslashes instead of slashes. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
An IPv4 host written in hexadecimal. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
An IPv6 host that is not in its RFC 5952 canonical form. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
A port with a leading zero. The SDKs refuse to sign such a URL and reject it with `url_not_normalized`.
The same request is verified twice with one nonce store: the second `(keyid, nonce)` is a replay.
